title: Poached White Peaches
subtitle: White peaches in a light elderflower and lemon syrup, served cold
excerpt: White peaches peeled and poached in a delicate elderflower and lemon syrup until just tender, served chilled with the scented syrup poured over. A light, elegant late-summer dessert.
sourceNotes: White peaches are sweeter and more fragrant than yellow varieties and need very little cooking, just enough to soften the flesh while keeping their shape. The elderflower syrup is a British summer flavour pairing that has become a fixture in restaurant kitchens since the 1990s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 6 hours ahead and serve chilled. The flavour of the elderflower and lemon concentrates as the peaches cool in the syrup.

content.text: Poached white peaches are a very gentle dessert, barely cooked, kept pale, in a syrup light enough that the peach flavour carries clearly. White peaches need about 10 to 15 minutes of poaching at most; longer and they become soft and lose their shape. Elderflower cordial gives the syrup a floral note that pairs well with the sweet, almost musky quality of white peaches. Serve very cold with just the syrup and, optionally, a little cream.

items.prepNote: white variety if possible, ripe but firm
peel in wide strips, plus the juice

content.text: Combine the water, sugar, lemon peel, and lemon juice in a saucepan wide enough to hold the peach halves in a single layer. Heat over a medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and stir in the elderflower cordial and vanilla bean paste if using.

Score a small cross in the base of each peach. Lower into the just-simmering syrup for 30 seconds, then transfer to a bowl of cold water. The skins will slip off easily. If the skins do not come away, return to the syrup for another 20 seconds. Once peeled, halve the peaches and remove the stones.

Return the syrup to a gentle simmer. Place the peach halves cut-side down in the syrup. Cover with a cartouche of baking paper. Poach over the lowest heat for 8 to 12 minutes until just tender when tested with a skewer, the flesh should give without collapsing. Riper peaches need only 8 minutes; firmer ones may need 12. Remove from the heat.

Transfer the peach halves to a shallow serving dish, cut-side up. Strain the syrup, discarding the lemon peel. Pour the syrup over the peaches. Leave to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving. Serve cold, with the syrup spooned over generously.

items.cause: They were over-ripe before cooking, or poached for too long.
items.fix: Use peaches that are ripe but still slightly firm to the touch. Check at 8 minutes and remove as soon as a skewer meets only gentle resistance.

items.symptom: The skins are not coming off easily
items.cause: The syrup was not hot enough when the peaches were blanched, or the variety has a very tough skin.
items.fix: Return to the hot syrup for another 20 to 30 seconds. Very ripe peaches skin easily; under-ripe ones may need a little more heat.

items.symptom: The elderflower flavour is lost in the finished dish
items.cause: Elderflower cordial's floral notes are delicate and can be overwhelmed if the syrup is reduced or the peaches are served warm.
items.fix: Add the cordial after taking the syrup off the heat, not during simmering. Serve cold so the elderflower fragrance is at its most apparent.

content.text: Keeps in the fridge, covered in syrup, for up to 2 days. The peaches soften further in storage; serve within 24 hours for the best texture.
